statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-116322 (PostgreSQL pre-authentication cancel request can leak a spinlock) affects only PostgreSQL 18: the PostgreSQL security page, https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116322/, says versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected and lists 18.7 as the only fixed release, and the CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-116322, lists only major version 18 as affected. The flaw is that, since PostgreSQL 18, a backend handling a cancel request before authentication compares cancel keys while holding a spinlock in shared memory, so an authentication_timeout or SIGTERM arriving at that moment exits with the lock held. That behaviour came from commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/9d9b9d46f3c509c722ebbf2a1e7dc6296a6c711d ("Move cancel key generation to after forking the backend", first released in PostgreSQL 18), and the fix, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/208ea05a51b8e2116323054aa5110f66803a010d, changes src/backend/tcop/backend_startup.c and is marked back-patch through 18. Commit 9d9b9d46 is not in any PostgreSQL 17 release. At every PostgreSQL 17 release this owner publishes (REL_17_7 through REL_17_12; for example https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_17_12/src/backend/tcop/backend_startup.c), a cancel request is handled by processCancelRequest, which looks up the target in the postmaster's backend list and signals it without taking any spinlock, and src/backend/storage/ipc/procsignal.c has neither the pss_mutex spinlock nor SendCancelRequest. The postgres server binary in every published DHI postgresql17 build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0) reports its 17.x release on both x86_64 and aarch64, and none of the Alpine patches applied in the 17.12-r0 APKBUILD touch connection startup or cancel handling. The 17.12 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/, do not list this CVE. Alpine's postgresql17 17.12-r0 secfixes list CVE-2026-116322 (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-116322), but upstream's own advisory places PostgreSQL 17 outside the affected range.
